I have an issue:
say I have multiple clients runnig on different terminals, 1 ns,  and1 ss:
client 1 calls a write commands on a sentence and does ctrl c midway (ie before ETIRW)
then neither of the clients are able to write on that sentence irrespective of whether client 1 reconnects or not
this is because when ctrl c happens, the lock for that sentence is not released, so none of the clients are able to write (not even client 1 when it starts running again)
How can I handle this issue?

message.text: Looking at client.c, looking in handle_write and sigint_handler and main function, tell me why the storage server is closing on temrinal if there is a ctrl c on a client while the write command was being handled.

parts.text: Looking at client.c, looking in handle_write and sigint_handler and main function, tell me why the storage server is closing on temrinal if there is a ctrl c on a client while the write command was being handled.

response.value:
GitHub Copilot

Short answer — what's happening and why:

- Your SIGINT handler calls send_message((int)current_ss_sock, &msg) and then _exit(1). send_message (and likely recv/send, string functions, logger, etc.) are not async‑signal‑safe. Calling them from a signal handler leads to undefined behavior and can corrupt the socket stream or internal libc state.
- If the handler does a partial/garbled send or interferes with the main thread that is also using the same ss_sock, the storage server receives malformed data and/or an unexpected stream state and closes the connection.
- After the handler calls _exit(1) the client process is abruptly terminated and the kernel closes all sockets. The SS therefore sees the TCP connection drop and that looks to the server like the client disconnected — the connection on the server side is closed.
- You also close client.nm_sock in the handler, again doing non‑safe operations in the handler and guaranteeing the client will not continue running to do a clean unlock/return to the prompt.

Consequences in your code:
- current_ss_sock / current_locked_sentence exist so you try to unlock in the handler, but send_message from a signal handler is unsafe. Race with handle_write (main thread) causes protocol corruption or partial writes. Then _exit closes sockets immediately.

Short fix recommendation:
- Do not call send_message/close/_exit in the signal handler.
- Make the handler async‑signal‑safe: write a byte to a self‑pipe (or set sig_atomic_t flag) and return.
- In handle_write (main thread) select/poll on stdin and the pipe; when the pipe is readable, perform the unlock over the SS socket from the main thread (safe), close the ss_sock and return to the prompt. This unlocks the sentence without terminating the client or causing corrupted socket traffic.

If you want, I can produce a small patch to implement the self‑pipe + select approach in your client.c.
